text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Ivan Peto was re-elected for another two-year term as party president at the Free Democrats' congress at the weekend. Prime Minister Gyula Horn sent a letter of congratulations to Peto. @
- Addressing the conference Economy '97, Prime Minister Gyula Horn said that economic growth could begin in 1997.
- Most leading members of the parliamentary group of the Socialists find it unacceptable that the bill on conflicts of interest will take effect retroactively, said Socialist MP Mihaly Bihari. @

- In a toughly worded press statement released from his hospital bedside, Minister of the Interior Gabor Kuncze criticised the police for failing to come up with any results from investigations into a recent spate of grenade blasts and murders. Interior Ministry sources believe the minister will relieve the Budapest police commander from his post.
- Democratic Federation of Hungarians in Romania president Bela Marko confirmed that his party will accept cabinet posts in the new coalition government at the ministerial level. @

- The whereabouts of Hungarian Ambassador Antal Annus, accredited to Kenya and also to Ethiopia, was unknown on Sunday after he boarded the ill-fated Boeing 767 which crashed into sea near the shores of Comoro Islands.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal has denied rumors that a group of high-ranking politicians are planning a putsch or have held consultations on a shake-up of the cabinet.
- Hungary's net debts decreased to $13.2 billion in September from previous month's $13.8 billion at current prices, reports the National Bank. @
- A bill presented to Parliament by the Finance Ministry Friday has established the range of applicants who can expect to receive a 1 percent cut of individual citizens' personal income tax. (Sat.)
- Around 300 tons of hazardous waste stored for months at the Letenye border station is to be returned to Germany in the middle of next week.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti is set to begin an official visit to Rome today. @
- Minister of Industry, Trade and Tourism Szabolcs Fazekas and Hans Eichel, Prime Minister of the German federal state of Hessen, agreed Friday to set up a joint economic committee.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Deputy general director in charge of finance Dr. Gabor Tompa was appointed to run the Hungarian News Agency MTI on a temporary basis.

- East European countries' answers to questionnaires concerning their economies, sent back to the European Union this summer, are too optimistic, mirroring expectations rather than facts, said European Commission President Jacques Santer. @
- The refrigeration company Goldsun, based in Zalaegerszeg, has received a warning from the EBRD to pay back the DM 6.3 million it owes the bank without delay.
- The London-based investment bank Nomura is encouraging investors to buy shares in the brewery Soproni Sorgyar, majority owned by the Austrian Brau Union.
- The operation of a new open-ended investment fund named Imperial-R has been approved by the State Supervision of Securities and Exchanges.
